channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] 36 years later: Hungary opens Communist-era secret service files
item.description: Decades after the end of Soviet rule, Hungary is releasing all its secret service files. The disclosure is sparking fresh debate about informants, guilt and responsibility.

item.title: [DW] Kosovo: Outrage as authorities accused of not helping femicide victim
item.description: Despite reporting her husband to the police and pleading for protection, Arlinda Zekaj was brutally murdered. Now, thousands in Kosovo are protesting what they say is a dramatic failure of state institutions.

item.title: [DW] Evacuation from Oleshky: How are preparations going?
item.description: A lawyer with the Save Ukraine Foundation, Myroslava Kharchenko, told DW about what has been happening in Russian-occupied Oleshky since a temporary ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump took effect.

item.title: [DW] EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
item.description: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.

item.title: [Financial Times] ‘The money didn’t work’: Big Tech’s $600mn midterm campaign falls flat
item.description: Elon Musk rebuked as anger at AI and Silicon Valley fuels support for Democrats

item.title: [Financial Times] Vance blames Iran war for crushing Republican midterms defeat
item.description: Oil prices tumble as Democrats’ landslide victory piles pressure on Donald Trump to end Middle East conflict

item.title: [Financial Times] ‘Rupert does not want to be with a loser’: Murdoch’s media empire cools on Trump
item.description: Fox News hosts question Iran war strategy while New York Post has ‘Blue Tsunami’ on front page after Republicans’ defeat

item.title: [Politico Europe] What’s bad for Trump is good for Le Pen
item.description: Anger at the rising cost of living spells danger for incumbents everywhere.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Spanish rail infrastructure chief steps down after Toledo train crash
item.description: It marks the second resignation related to the disaster in just 24 hours.

item.title: [Financial Times] How Democrats pulled off the blue wave in maps and charts
item.description: Party on track for largest swing in their favour in House elections in more than 75 years

item.title: [EU Observer] Two fatal train disasters in less than a year: I never thought I would see this happen in my native Spain
item.description: As Spain’s transport minister resigns and politicians trade accusations over budgets and responsibility, many ordinary Spaniards are left wondering why the safety systems failed - and how the country could suffer 115 railway deaths in a single year.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Hungary releases secret police files from communist era
item.description: The files reveal the names of the socialist regime's informant network, 70 years after the Soviet Union crushed the Hungarian revolution of 1956.

item.title: [Financial Times] Voters have put a helpful chill on the US data centre boom
item.description: Midterm results could affect 45 per cent of planned expansion, but there is a silver lining for investors

item.title: [Politico Europe] MEPs fear fundamental rights will take a hit under plans to expand EU border agency
item.description: New mandate would permit Frontex to support deportations to and from return hubs, commissioner says.

item.title: [Financial Times] Republicans turn on each other after disastrous midterms
item.description: Party figures lash out at Donald Trump, his candidates and his staff over Iran war, cost of living and corruption allegations

item.title: [Financial Times] The party’s over for the Trumpsterz
item.description: Dancing gives way to dejection at Florida festivities

item.title: [Politico Europe] Midterms : 5 points que l’Europe doit surveiller après l’écrasante victoire des démocrates face à Trump
item.description: Du Texas à l'Ohio, les républicains ont connu une soirée électorale catastrophique. Quel sera l'impact de ces résultats sur l'Europe ?

item.title: [Euractiv] Environment MEPs oppose ‘unlawful’ EU approval for shipbreaking on Indian beaches
item.description: Bad for workers, the environment and ‘a death sentence for European ship recyclers’, one lawmaker says

item.title: [Financial Times] The beginning of the end of the age of Trump
item.description: A stunning rebuke by Americans offers a chance to start rebuilding US democracy

item.title: [EU Observer] Afghan pushback survivor fights ‘impossible’ evidence rules in European courts with new UN case against Greece
item.description: The EU's human rights court rejected a case from an Afghan pushback survivor who was just 15 years old when he was turned back to Turkey by the Hellenic coast guard. The impossibility of achieving justice on the systematic practice against migrants of all ages was highlighted by the European court's inadmission, as the young survivor was forced to appeal to the UN's human rights courts instead.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Damaged Chernobyl nuclear site needs urgent funding, warns European development bank
item.description: Half a billion euros is required to fix the protective dome that was damaged by Russian attacks.

item.title: [Euractiv] EU, NATO split roles in Brussels talks on Ukraine
item.description: A two-track structure emerges for EU-US-NATO ahead of next week's Abu Dhabi summit

item.title: [Euractiv] CAP cuts would hit smaller farms, livestock producers hardest
item.description: New study warns proposed EU farm funding cuts would hit beef and sheep producers particularly hard

item.title: [EU Observer] Moldova seen as ‘best performer’ on EU-accession reforms, despite onslaught of Russian sabotage
item.description: Chișinău's progress took place against a backdrop of growing hybrid attacks from Russia, such as drones entering the country’s airspace, cyberattacks, and Moldovan citizens recruited to perform sabotage.

item.title: [Euractiv] Conscious uncoupling
item.description: Tonight's edition also includes: Stalling Ukraine-Europe talks on alternatives to Starlink

item.title: [Euractiv] Ukraine’s IMF loan hinges on new EU funding, Brussels warns
item.description: Divided EU leaders are scrambling to secure €45 billion in additional funding for Kyiv

item.title: [EU Observer] Russia fails in bid to reverse ban on its ships using Europe’s docks and locks
item.description: Russian authorities challenged restrictive measures imposed by EU ministers against ships approved by the St Petersburg ship-certifying body. The EU's General Court rejected a bid to overturn the ban, but left the door open for future recognition of the authority.

item.title: [EU Observer] Energy tax and carbon emissions law on chopping block as EU Commission doubles down on ‘simplification’ drive
item.description: More than 30 laws will be mothballed or repealed, the EU Commission announced on Wednesday, as its deregulation agenda continues to gather pace.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Mélenchon a-t-il déjà son ticket pour le second tour ?
item.description: La France insoumise s’est réjouie de la défaite de Donald Trump lors des élections de mi-mandat aux Etats-Unis, y voyant la possibilité de “faire reculer l’extrême droite”. Toute coïncidence avec la situation française n’est pas fortuite, alors que le scénario d’un second tour opposant Marine Le Pen à Jean-Luc Mélenchon devient de plus en plus […]

item.title: [Euractiv] MEPs push to overhaul EU cross-border healthcare rules
item.description: Rare disease patients face financial and bureaucratic barriers to accessing treatment abroad

item.title: [Financial Times] Democrats debate how far to take their fight against Trump
item.description: Even with control of both the Senate and the House, Democratic legislation could still be obstructed by presidential veto

item.title: [Euractiv] Centrist MEPs agree on reversal of petrol, diesel car ban
item.description: Greens' negotiator warns of investment risk from "political flip-flopping"

item.title: [EU Observer] Lame duck or angry duck? Europe’s leadership largely silent on Trump’s election disaster, fearing backlash
item.description: Sweeping US mid-term election wins by the Democrats have earned only muted or scattered responses and reactions from Europe's leadership.

item.title: [Euractiv] No date for Ukraine’s EU entry
item.description: War-torn Ukraine is behind Moldova in the race to finish EU membership negotiations

item.title: [Euractiv] First EU-wide space regulation gets handshake deal in Parliament
item.description: The final text still needs to be written before going to a full vote

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] ‘It’s now or never’ for enlargement, Montenegro’s former EU ambassador warns
item.description: "With the Russian intervention in Ukraine, the geopolitical situation changed dramatically ... the EU understood they have to fortify 'their territory' in south-eastern Europe, and now you have, again, full energy [in the enlargement process]," Bojan Šarkić said.

item.title: [EU Observer] Roma ‘intimidation’ in Bulgarian presidentials as Iliana Iotova’s win raises alarm bells for press freedom
item.description: Iliana Iotova's election win in Bulgaria's presidential run-off has analysts worried about her relationship with Russia and attitude towards democratic freedoms. She is expected to align with prime minister Rumen Radev.

item.title: [Financial Times] How the Trump era crashed
item.description: The US president forgot the economic bit of populism

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: What is Europe’s military exercise in Poland really for?
item.description: A large-scale military exercise is about to begin in Poland, starting Monday, 9 October. The coalition of the willing is testing how their forces work together and sending a political message supporting Ukraine.

item.title: [EU Observer] It’s not a coup: Tusk is right to reclaim Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal, but wrong in how he is doing it
item.description: Donald Tusk has a legal duty to rebuild Poland’s captured Constitutional Tribunal. But the government’s handling of the latest confrontation and its own appointments risks turning a victory for the rule of law into a political defeat, writes Alberto Alemanno.

item.title: [EU Observer] Is the Western Sahara now friendless? No, EU backing for Morocco is conditional, and Spanish election will be pivotal
item.description: Spain's general election could be, in part, a referendum on the country's partnership with Morocco, with the opposition promising tougher border control measures and closer ties with Rabat's neighbour and enemy, Algeria.

item.title: [DW] Cyprus: From ties with Russia to a strategic alignment with the US
item.description: The Republic of Cyprus long balanced ties between Russia and the West. Now, it is phasing out Russian weapons, expanding defense cooperation with the United States and redefining its place in the Eastern Mediterranean.

item.title: [DW] Multiple flights to European airports targeted by bomb threats
item.description: The bomb threats involved two passenger planes bound for Warsaw, a Ryanair flight from London to Spain, two flights to Rome and a flight traveling from Israel to the Bulgarian capital, Sofia. No explosives were found.

item.title: [DW] Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?
item.description: France, Germany and Italy face a volatile bond market as war inflation bites. With US tech giants now issuing billions in AI bonds, they are competing with cash-strapped European governments.

item.title: [EU Observer] What Cary, a small town in North Carolina, means for US mid-term elections and everyone else in Europe
item.description: Cary is just a small town in North Carolina. But it is also part of a larger campaign by the Democrats to take over the Senate during this mid-term election.

item.title: [EU Observer] Czech public broadcasters hold historic strike following government vote to abolish licence fees
item.description: Thousand of Czechs joined public TV and radio workers in their walkout over the Czech government's moves to bring public broadcasting under its political control.

item.title: [EU Observer] Firefighters from 19 countries protest EU budget cuts in Brussels
item.description: Around 1,000 firefighters from 19 countries gathered in Brussels Tuesday to demand more equipment, more staff, and adequate healthcare, only weeks before key EU budget negotiations.

item.title: [EU Observer] Trump likely to lash out in foreign policy if Democrats take Congress, warns ex-US ambassador to EU
item.description: Being hamstrung by a Democrat Congress could embolden Donald Trump to become even more radical on foreign policy.

item.title: [DW] European Central Bank (ECB) head Christine Lagarde to step down in February, before her term ends
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde is to resign nine months ahead of the end of her 8-year term. European Council President Antonio Costa has said the process to find a successor is underway.

item.description: POLITICAL ADVERTISEMENT More information here.

item.description: Hyperscalers surge and chipmakers fall as investors bet on winners and losers from expected backlash against the AI boom

item.description: US vice-president JD Vance blames Republicans’ midterm defeat on anger over Iran war

item.title: [Euractiv] Mélenchon’s next mission for young voters: convince your parents
item.description: The far-left leader is mobilising Gen-Z supporters to take his campaign to family dinner tables across France

item.title: [Euractiv] French dentists fired over Chinese prostheses take legal action
item.description: Dentists say their employer put profits before patients by demanding they source 30% of dental prostheses from China

item.title: [Euractiv] The midterms won’t save Europe
item.description: If Trump didn’t respect a Republican-controlled Congress, he will value a Democrat-led Congress even less

item.title: [Euractiv] Conservationists despair as EU presses ahead with nature law review
item.description: Review of Birds and Habitats Directives goes ahead despite million-strong petition, scientists' warnings and objections from major EU capitals

item.title: [Euractiv] Ukraine aid cannot hinge on EU budget, says Finland
item.description: EU must be ready to finance Ukraine whatever happens with fraught and protracted budget talks

item.title: [Euractiv] Capitals up in arms at EU freeze on national social media bans
item.description: "We cannot wait. It will take a long time before the new rules have a real-world impact, and we have already been waiting for the Commission for a year.”

item.title: [Politico Europe] Le Pen keeps Farage hanging over his Paris rendezvous
item.description: The two right-wing leaders were meant to meet in October — but the dynamics in both their parties have shifted.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Canada spat exposes widening rift between Merz and von der Leyen
item.description: Berlin’s effort to reserve associate status for Kyiv has collided with the Commission president’s Ottawa initiative.

item.title: [Financial Times] US midterm results herald upheaval in Middle East policy
item.description: American voters — including vice-president JD Vance — want an end to Trump’s Iran war and Washington’s proximity to Israel

item.title: [Financial Times] Democratic wave keeps US wealth taxes on the agenda despite California setback
item.description: Proposition 40 billionaire tax set to be defeated in a rare victory for mega-donors in the US midterms

item.title: [DW] Russia's giant new radar in Kaliningrad raises alarm in NATO
item.description: Russia is nearing completion of what experts think is a giant radar complex in Kaliningrad, capable of monitoring much of Europe. Experts warn the project could intensify the military standoff between Moscow and NATO.

item.title: [DW] Ethnic Germans in Kazakhstan face legacy of the Soviet Union
item.description: Kazakhstan is struggling to deal with the legacy of the Soviet dictatorship. Some 85 years ago, Stalin deported hundreds of thousands of people: Some 400,000 ethnic Germans living in the USSR were sent to Kazakhstan.

item.title: [DW] Serbia after Vucic: The winners are losing patience
item.description: After the Student List's election victory, Aleksandar Vucic's power apparatus is disintegrating. People want justice as soon as possible. But the losers still hold sway in the judiciary and administration.

item.title: [DW] Global pedestrian Karl Bushby returns home to UK after 28-year trek
item.description: Karl Bushby, a British man who traveled 50,000 km without transport over the past 28 years, has come home. Starting in Chile, he crossed the Americas, Russia and parts of Central Asia and Europe — almost all on foot.

item.title: [DW] How Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria
item.description: Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria, promising to be a "president of peace." But the campaign showed how divided Bulgarians are about the war in Ukraine and drone attacks in the Black Sea.

item.title: [DW] Canadian PM Mark Carney discusses talks with the EU, overdependence on the US and how to deal with Donald Trump in a DW interview.
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney tells DW that Canada is seeking closer EU ties to "diversify and deepen" partnerships beyond the Americas. Despite German pushback, he said he favors the all-new term "associate membership."

item.title: [DW] What the rift within the Tsikhanouski family means for the Belarusian opposition in exile
item.description: Siarhei Tsikhanouski criticizes the work of his wife, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, and her office. He also questions her legitimacy. What are the implications for Belarusian political forces in exile?
